summary: PASS. My round-5 finding F-DG4-145 verifies CLOSED. The controlled Date.now clock makes the Y1c /me count deterministic: the session files pass 80/80 in 8 contended pnpm test runs (load 20-30, and held at 13-15). In the pinned reproduction, the count never fails on the candidate, while the pre-repair file fails 2/2; the same file without its clock also fails 2/2. Mutants M1/M2/M3/M5 of the identity rules are killed. The full review is green: 7/7 static checks; pnpm test 4/4 at low load; integration 1975/1975 twice (61 migrations, contract.test.ts, 0 pending); tests/qa 172/172; REQ-DLV-036 85/85; both full e2e runs with all 364 tests counted and every failure passing solo; my probes at 546+77+14 checks per language with 0 failed; validator 5/5; trace 137/137. Three new non-blocking Low findings, all about test determinism and coverage, none a product defect: F-DG4-146 (no test pins 'page GETs wait for the /me in flight'; mutant M4 survives); F-DG4-147 (session-end.spec.ts '403' races the SPA's boot /me); F-DG4-148 (pnpm test first-render timeouts at load >= 13). Every non-pass is disclosed in RUN-NOTES.md. No product gate (G1-G6) was decided, and G6 never implies DG7.
